sources.title: Introduction
sources.finding: Augment distinguishes Cosmos automations, Auggie CLI and VS Code/JetBrains integrations; capabilities are not inherited across clients.

sources.title: Getting started with Cosmos
sources.finding: Cosmos runs Experts in sandboxed VMs with triggers, private/shared sessions and persistent automation rules.

sources.title: Augment Code homepage
sources.locator: Start from anything; run anywhere; humans; memory
sources.finding: The vendor advertises managed and user-owned execution, shared memory, expert handoffs and human checkpoints. These claims were not exercised.

sources.title: Introducing Auggie CLI
sources.finding: The 1.x docs describe a prerelease CLI requiring Node 20+, account login, local indexing and print/stream/JSON automation modes.

sources.title: Augment pricing
sources.locator: Plan cards; usage FAQ checked 7 November 2026
sources.finding: Standard and Business are flat team prices with pooled dollar usage; LLM API list price has a 40% service fee and compute is separate.

sources.title: Augment changelog
sources.finding: Release notes state agents no longer merge PRs, session cost visibility is admin-only, snapshots last fourteen days, and analytics can export CSV.

sources.title: Augment Code homepage
sources.locator: Title; Harness announcement banner; PR Author; footer
sources.finding: The page retains the Augment Code name, links the Harness announcement and credits Harness, Inc. in its footer. PR Author is described as driving work through merge without naming who executes the merge.

sources.title: Harness acquires Augment Code to advance the Autonomous SDLC
sources.locator: Published 8 October 2026, updated 19 October; acquisition; What makes Harness Cosmos; Get started
sources.finding: Harness says it acquired selected Augment assets, names Cosmos the Harness Cosmos Software Factory Agent and says it is available now. Agents prepare changes for a team merge decision.

sources.title: PR to Merge
sources.locator: How it works; Where you participate
sources.finding: Experts review and repair changes. A human decides and performs the final merge. Configured agent approval is separate from merging.

sources.title: PR Author
sources.finding: PR Author creates a branch, implements the change, opens a PR or MR and handles CI, merge conflicts and review comments.

sources.title: Cosmos Week 38 Release Notes
sources.finding: The release note explicitly removes agent pull-request merging.

sources.title: Using Sessions
sources.locator: About sessions; Session lifecycle; Share a session
sources.finding: Cosmos supports phone browsers, explicitly has no separate iOS/Android app, saves conversations indefinitely, and gives individually shared users viewer access. Environments pause and may restart clean.

sources.title: Using Tasklist
sources.locator: Creating a New Task; Subtasks; Status; Reviewing Changes
sources.finding: IDE Tasklist supports human and agent creation, editable nested tasks, explicit execution, state indicators, moving lists to a new chat and per-task diff review.

sources.title: Project Builder
sources.finding: The Expert drafts a design, iterates with the human, breaks work into tickets and launches PR Author workers in dependency waves. It never writes implementation code or merges.

sources.title: Auggie Subagents
sources.finding: Built-in and custom subagents have independent context, tools and prompts, run concurrently and report progress in the parent thread. Configuration includes model and thinking level.

sources.title: Daemon Workspaces and Isolation
sources.finding: Isolated daemon sessions get one Git worktree per repository. Shared sessions edit the daemon checkout and may overwrite each other. Isolation requires Git 2.31+.

sources.title: Install Auggie CLI
sources.finding: Auggie runs locally or on a server with Node 20+, macOS, Linux or Windows WSL and zsh/bash/fish. Version 1 is prerelease; stable 0.x remains available.

sources.title: PR Author
sources.finding: PR Author creates branches and pull or merge requests, follows CI, handles merge conflicts and responds to review comments.

sources.title: Using Teams
sources.finding: Administrator manages invites, members, seats, plan and billing. Member can view team information or leave, but cannot administer billing or membership.

sources.title: Augment Code Pricing
sources.locator: Plan cards; Usage FAQ; Support FAQ
sources.finding: Standard is $20/month for up to 50 seats with $20 shared usage; Business is $100. LLM list rates plus 40% service fee, compute without that fee, pooled top-ups valid twelve months. Trials exclude SLA.

sources.title: Available Models
sources.finding: Augment lists Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, DeepSeek, Zhipu, xAI and Moonshot models, subject to organization configuration; model options do not prove external harness support.

sources.title: Augment Code introduction.md
sources.locator: Cosmos, Auggie CLI, IDE clients; linked current model/subagent documentation
sources.finding: The introduction distinguishes the Cosmos automation product, Auggie CLI and Augment IDE clients. The coding workflow is supplied by Augment/Auggie and Cosmos experts; selected Anthropic/OpenAI/Google/xAI model providers do not run those vendors coding CLI harnesses.

sources.title: Augment Code professional terms of service
sources.finding: The main software-engineering AI platform is covered by Augment professional terms. Customer access is non-exclusive/non-transferable and limited to internal business use; distribution, reverse engineering and derivative versions are restricted, and the company retains platform intellectual property.
